notes: Serial-process studies assign upgrades in queue order. Shares are the percentages stated in each project's Facilities Study (or SIS where noted); dollar figures are FaS values.
Every Phoenix Metro serial project is battery storage except Q394. Most carry only POI switchyard work; the system upgrades are short 69 kV rebuilds.

Two shared totals are back-calculated from a stated share (marked *): Deer Valley–Yorkshire Tap (~$0.79M, six projects, including in-service Q278 and Q292 whose shares aren't shown) and the Raceway 230 kV expansion (~$6.2M, mostly on in-service Q278 and withdrawn Q287).

Cluster 4 SIS also assigned a 2nd Freedom 230/69 kV transformer ($5.0M) 100% to Q357 (Freedom 69 kV, now COD/pending refund, mapped to Gila Bend). The Freedom–West Park 69 kV rebuild is APS responsibility; neither is shown.
Later MMAs for Q268 (2024), Q299 (2025) and Q363 (2025) changed inverters or phasing only and added no network upgrades. MMAs for in-service Q229 and Q314 likewise added none.
view_note: Ten serial projects (1,305 MW, almost all battery storage) sit ahead of the cluster in Phoenix Metro. Their system upgrade shares come to about $7M, all short 69 kV rebuilds and station work. Q299 alone carries $4.0M for two Westwing-area 69 kV lines; the Deer Valley–Yorkshire and Raceway shares stay deferred until other projects build. Q355's Liberty 230 kV share was dropped in its Facilities Study.
full_note: The serial queue in Phoenix Metro left little shared transmission behind: about $7M of allocated 69 kV and station work, mostly deferred or single-project. The cluster rows below carry the area's larger upgrades.
